| [CASE-337](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-337.md) | Beta–Bernoulli features vs shared-driver null | [LEAD-144](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-144.md)'s study, the "Option A" [CASE-165](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-165.md) recommends, in one linear family. Twenty-four members in six overlapping working groups, with a communication graph built from the groups, are simulated in three worlds: coupled along the graph; driven by one persistent external driver per group with no interaction; and half of each. The driver's gain is tuned so that every world shows the same within-group correlation, 0.30. CASE-165's finite beta-Bernoulli model (K = 16, α = 3) and four comparators are fitted to 600 days of each world and scored on interventions none was fitted to: a pulse to a member, and the cut of a group's internal ties. Over seven organizations, the feature model finds more features under the null (11.1) than under coupling (8.7), better aligned with the groups (Jaccard 0.72 against 0.44); read as causes of members it is exact under the driver and misses every cut under coupling, and read as realized by its holders it is wrong in both. The communication graph alone is right under coupling and invents coupling under the driver (a predicted cut effect of −0.18 where the truth is 0); the features added to it leave that error (0.21), and observing the true driver removes it (0.006). One-step fit ranks the models the same way in every world. The design, code and wording are the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

Exact enumeration per content and 4,000-replication simulations of correlated rank-2 systems at 2 to 100 occurrences a context. The plug-in Δ's bias at zero signalling is 1.5 at two occurrences and 0.22 at a hundred; the root of the unbiased squared difference cuts it by half or more and falls short at large Δ. | [CASE-398](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-398.md) | Logit subspaces in GPT-2 small and Pythia-70m | [LEAD-073](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-073.md) asked for [NOTE-746](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-746.md)'s M, N and Γ_q in released models, for relations where linearity has been reported. Forward passes of GPT-2 small and Pythia-70m, in numpy on CPU, gave the final-layer-norm output f(x) over about 3,200 contexts, and the unembeddings gave G. Exactly, both models meet the diversity condition: the unembeddings span the whole space, and the final layer norm's bias leaves every f(x) with a fixed nonzero component off the hyperplane its normalisation confines it to, so F is the whole space too. Then M = N = ℝᵈ and the containments Γ ⊆ N and Γ_q ⊆ M hold for any relation. At the tolerance stated before the run (singular values above 1e-3 of the largest; at most 1% of any direction outside), they fail for all three relations tested (city in country, country language, country capital) in GPT-2 small, whose context spectrum is dominated by one direction, and fail narrowly for Γ ⊆ N in Pythia-70m, where f is constant, to within 2.4e-4, along one direction. A post-hoc sweep shows the verdict turning on the tolerance. City in country is fairly linear in GPT-2 small (held-out R² 0.82); the other relations less so. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CASE-402](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-402.md) v2 | SGD vs the 6-gon in the toy superposition model | [LEAD-175](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-175.md) asked for the two tests [QUESTION-363](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-363.md)'s note of 2026-11-06 moved there from [THEORY-1275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1275.md): SGD at n = 1,000 and on both sides of n ≈ 600 across rates, batch sizes and initialisations, to see whether the 6-gon is reached; and posterior sampling across n to check the critical sample sizes the free-energy formula gives for the chain 4⁺⁺⁻ → 4⁺ → 5 → 5⁺. In the model of Chen et al. ([LIT-1894](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1894.md)), in numpy: no SGD run reached the 6-gon. The 5-gon's dropped feature gets an exactly zero gradient from every sample, so SGD cannot move it at any setting. The 5⁺-gon is a live local minimum that SGD does not leave in 45,000 epochs. Sampling exp(−nL) under the N(0, 1) prior puts 5 → 6 at n ≈ 265–279 and 5 → 5⁺ at n ≈ 780. The first two steps of the chain have no crossing above n ≈ 1. Chen et al.'s NUTS likelihood carries a factor ½ that their formula's nL does not, so their sample size is twice these n; on that scale the sampled 5 → 6 is at about 530–560, consistent with their Fig. 2. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
